results: 1. Measure visual acuity in each eye separately with appropriate refractive correction.
not performed / not available
2. Perform a complete ocular motility examination in all diagnostic positions of gaze, including assessment for nystagmus and diplopia.
nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze: no nystagmus
smooth pursuit and saccades: normal
adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): on left gaze the right eye fails to adduct, and the contralateral eye shows NO abducting nystagmus - unlike a classic INO
abducting nystagmus of the fellow eye: absent
vertical gaze and convergence: mild vertical limitation and mildly impaired convergence
ocular torsion and head tilt: none
3. Perform cover–uncover and alternate-cover testing at distance and near.
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
4. Examine the pupils for size, symmetry, and direct and consensual light responses.
pupil size and light reaction: pupils EQUALLY REACTIVE - pupil-sparing
5. Measure and document upper-eyelid position, ptosis, levator function, and orbicularis strength.
ptosis / lid position: partial ptosis
6. Assess ocular motility and ptosis before and after sustained upgaze and repeated blinking.
nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze: no nystagmus
smooth pursuit and saccades: normal
adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): on left gaze the right eye fails to adduct, and the contralateral eye shows NO abducting nystagmus - unlike a classic INO
abducting nystagmus of the fellow eye: absent
vertical gaze and convergence: mild vertical limitation and mildly impaired convergence
ptosis / lid position: partial ptosis
7. Perform an ice-pack test for ocular myasthenia gravis.
not performed / not available
8. Perform a complete neurologic examination, including cranial nerves, limb strength, reflexes, sensation, and cerebellar function.
cranial nerve examination: partial right oculomotor palsy with right adduction failure, mild vertical gaze limitation, mildly impaired convergence, and partial ptosis; pupils equally reactive
mental status / cognitive screen: normal
muscle tone examination: normal
limb strength (MRC) examination: normal
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): normal
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal
posture and pull test: normal
limb and truncal ataxia: absent
gait and tandem walking: normal
hearing and tinnitus: normal
9. Perform slit-lamp examination and dilated fundus examination.
fundoscopy: normal
10. Obtain serum acetylcholine-receptor antibodies and MuSK antibodies.
acetylcholine receptor, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies: normal
anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies: negative
11. Obtain thyroid-stimulating hormone and free thyroxine levels.
TSH / free T4: normal
12. Obtain an MRI of the brain, brainstem, and orbits with and without contrast.
MRI brain with gadolinium: small dorsal paramedian midbrain infarct
MRI sella and orbits: normal pituitary and orbits
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Partial pupil-sparing right oculomotor nerve palsy caused by a small dorsal paramedian midbrain ischemic infarct.

ALTERNATIVE: Seronegative ocular myasthenia gravis.

ALTERNATIVE: Demyelinating lesion of the midbrain affecting the oculomotor fascicles.

ALTERNATIVE: Small compressive midbrain lesion not detected on current imaging.
